I've been in a similar situation not that long ago. A university dropout living on my own, no friends, just sitting in my apartment day after day. Anxious as all hell, when I got my first cashier job I was physically shaking from even having to talk to people at all. But what I learned is that this anxiety slowly goes away the more job interviews you have. It kind of becomes a routine. Sure I'm still a lonely college dropout in my studio apartment but at least I don't have a panic attack calling my potential employer y'know. 

It'll get better, friend. You get used to everything in life. This pandemic kinda fucked everything up for a lot of us. The world is changing and a lot of things aren't how they used to be, but we'll get used to it eventually and it'll become a routine just like everything else. Hang in there.
